NO. 046 · Hunters of the Sky / Accipitridae · Hawks & Eagles

Black Kite

黑鸢 · hēi yuān Milvus migrans
Resident / winter visitor Common 54–69 cm Protected (Class II) IUCN LC

The 'eagle' you are most likely to see over Zhuhai

Look up anywhere in Zhuhai and the raptor you see is probably this one: dark brown body, pale forked tail, two big white patches under the wings. It rides the air for twenty minutes without a single wingbeat, turning like a sheet of paper in the sky.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • TailShallowly forked — not the deep fork of a swallow — and constantly twisted in flight to adjust direction. The most characteristic piece of the bird's behaviour.
  • UnderwingA large white patch at the base of the primaries beneath each wing forms two unmistakable 'light bulbs', visible at long range.
  • ColourDark brown throughout, paler on the head, with considerable individual variation; bill black, cere yellow.
  • FlightSoars with the wings in a shallow V and the primaries spread into obvious 'fingers'.

Behaviour

A thorough opportunist: it takes fish, rodents and birds, and feeds heavily on carrion and human refuse, gathering around city landfill sites and fishing harbours. It uses thermals to stay aloft for long periods on a light, drifting flight action. South China holds both residents and birds that move south in winter. It nests on cliffs, on high-voltage pylons and in large trees.

A horse-like whinny, 'pee-ee-ee' or 'hi-yah', tremulous, loud and far-carrying.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • skies over Banzhang Hill
  • Qi'ao Island
  • Jinwan seashore
  • high over the city
Field note
'Forked tail, two white patches beneath, shallow V wings' — that is the Black Kite hat-trick. A fan-shaped tail and no white underwing patches points to Eastern Buzzard or another hawk.
